title: Compliance trail incompleteness during identity-proxy key rollover
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: During a scheduled encryption key rollover for the identity-proxy (2025-02-18 02:30 UTC), a subset of audit events failed to persist to the compliance trail for roughly 12 minutes. The missing records were primarily authentication success/failure events associated with cross-region SSO redirects. This ticket consolidates the follow-up actions, verification steps, and decisions from the incident review.
timeline: 2025-02-18 02:30 UTC - Key rollover triggered; 02:33 UTC - identity-proxy instances began TLS renegotiation; 02:36 UTC - audit-ingest ACK timeouts observed; 02:42 UTC - log-sharder backpressure increased and dropped buffered batches; 02:44 UTC - alerts fired (audit-missing-rate, ingest-latency); 02:48 UTC - temporary mitigation: extended ack timeout and toggled synchronous flush; 02:52 UTC - full persistence restored; 02:55 UTC - post-incident verification and gap re-ingest started; 03:10 UTC - gap re-ingest completed for 98% of expected events.
root_cause: The rollover exposed a race between the identity-proxy's TLS session re-establishment and the audit-ingest's acknowledgement window. When multiple proxies rekeyed concurrently during the rolling update, a subset of ingesters hit a transient buffer-overflow path in log-sharder which discarded un-acked batches. The log transport previously relied on best-effort buffering without durable on-disk ack metadata for in-flight batches during a key transition.
impact_summary: Compliance trail incompleteness for ~12 minutes affecting cross-region SSO auth events. Estimated missing event count: ~4.2k, of which 98% were recovered by re-ingest. No customer PII exfiltration detected. Affected customers: 17 customers had degraded audit fidelity, two enterprise customers requested formal evidence of recovery and timeline.
detection_and_alerting: Detected by alert rule audit-missing-rate and manual investigations from on-call. Datadog dashboard link: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/audit-ingest-overview (internal). Pager duty runbook was followed; initial mitigation executed by infra on-call.
short_term_mitigation_taken: 1) Increased ingest ack timeout to prevent premature drops. 2) Disabled concurrent proxy-wide rekey scheduling; switched to instance-staggered rekey. 3) Launched re-ingest job to backfill gaps from buffer store and proxy local logs. 4) Notified affected customers and SOC for compliance documentation.
long_term_root_fix_proposal: 1) Implement durable ack metadata on log-sharder (persist in local WAL) so in-flight batches survive proxy restarts/rekeys. 2) Add reorder-safe handoff between identity-proxy and audit-ingest that tolerates TLS renegotiation. 3) Add chaos tests simulating concurrent key rotation and sharder pressure to CI. 4) Change default key-roll schedule to instance-staggered with guard windows for high-traffic regions.
action_items: AI-1: Implement WAL-backed ack persistence in log-sharder; owner: Arjun Patel; due: 2025-03-12; status: In Progress; linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-sharder/pull/89

AI-2: Add 'rekey-grace' handshake to identity-proxy to delay final ack until persistent write confirmed; owner: Lian Chen; due: 2025-03-05; status: Planned; RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/2025/rekey-grace.md
AI-3: Enforce instance-staggered key rollover orchestration in infra orchestrator; owner: SRE Team; due: 2025-03-02; status: Done; change: infra-orch v2.7.1
AI-4: Create CI chaos test for concurrent rekey + high ingest load; owner: Reliability QA; due: 2025-03-20; status: Planned; job: qa/chaos/rekey-ingest.yml

AI-5: Produce compliance evidence pack for impacted customers (timeline, recovered counts, dashboards); owner: Compliance Team (Elena Rossi); due: 2025-02-28; status: In Progress; artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_compliance_pack
AI-6: Postmortem write-up and exec summary for security review board; owner: Maya Thompson; due: 2025-02-26; status: Done; link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/ENG-27910+postmortem
verification_plan: 1) Run end-to-end synthetic that performs SSO auths across regions during staged rekey and validates all events land in audit store. 2) Add a 'no-gap' sweep daily for 14 days that compares proxy logs vs. audit store and flags mismatches. 3) Provide proof-of-fix dashboard and customer evidence pack to Compliance and affected accounts.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Durable WAL improves reliability but adds disk I/O and complexity for sharder horizontal scaling; need to design compaction/expiry. Staggered rollouts increase rollout time for critical CVEs; we must balance security urgency vs. audit fidelity. Chaos tests add CI runtime cost.
